name: Ryver
description: Ryver is a team communication and task-management service with teams, forums, chats, topics, tasks, boards, custom integrations, bots, webhooks, and a REST API.
agentUseSummary: Ryver cannot currently be connected because its general REST API still documents Basic Auth with a user's full account credential, not delegated OAuth. Its safer automation model is a customer-created Custom Integration user with manually generated tokens and selected team/forum installation, which is a distinct user-owned identity product requiring explicit approval.

blocked.label: Connect through delegated OAuth
blocked.description: Ryver's official v1 API documentation still says the general API uses Basic Auth and does not provide a current delegated OAuth lifecycle.

blocked.label: Use a user's password
blocked.description: Basic Auth would give Relay the user's full organization credential and effective account authority and is not an acceptable delegated connection.

blocked.label: Use a Custom Integration
blocked.description: A customer-created integration has its own user, selected team/forum membership, manually generated tokens, and optional bot/webhooks, requiring a separately approved user-owned product.

blocked.label: Access Ryver data
blocked.description: Organizations, users, teams, forums, chats, messages, topics, posts, tasks, boards, membership, administration, webhooks, arbitrary OData, and every read or write remain unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent action can be enabled until Relay approves a customer-owned Custom Integration identity or Ryver publishes a delegated OAuth contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No approved Ryver identity, credential, or wrapper contract is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No approved Ryver identity, credential, or wrapper contract is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Ryver offers unsafe user Basic Auth or a customer-owned Custom Integration user/token model, not a current delegated Relay-owned OAuth contract.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request a user password or integration token and do not show Connect. Reconsider after an explicit product/security decision approves a least-privilege Custom Integration, or after Ryver publishes a delegated consent and revocation contract.

evidence.supports: Ryver's official v1 API documentation states that the REST API currently uses Basic Auth and that OAuth or API-token support was future intent.
Ryver directs automation through customer-created Custom Integrations with a dedicated integration user, selected team/forum installation, webhooks, and one or more optionally expiring access tokens.
Ryver's API exposes broad reads and mutations over teams, forums, users, messages, topics, tasks, membership, and administrative operations.
Ryver bots operate as customer-defined integration identities rather than user-consented delegated OAuth applications.
